properties.areaDesc: Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast
properties.headline: Blizzard Warning issued November 9 at 7:33PM AKST until November 11 at 6:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions expected. Total snow accumulations up to
4 inches. Winds gusting as high as 55 mph.

* WHERE...Central Beaufort Sea Coast & Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM AKST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult at times. Areas of blowing
snow will significantly reduce visibility. Strong winds could
result in some power outages. Visibilities dropping to as low as
1/4 mile or less are expected at times, resulting in blizzard
conditions, depending on the intensity of the falling snow & the
severity of the blowing snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...East-northeast winds will increase as we
progress into Tuesday & generally remain stronger through midweek.
Scattered light snow showers are expected to continue during this
timeframe with the blizzard conditions most likely to start along
with the onset of steadier snowfall & heavier snowfall rates, which
will occur from late tonight through Tuesday & last through Tuesday
night.
properties.instruction:
A Blizzard Warning means severe winter weather conditions are
expected or occurring. Falling and blowing snow with strong winds are
likely. This will lead to whiteout conditions, making travel
extremely dangerous. If you must travel, have a winter survival kit
with you. If you get stranded, stay in your vehicle.

NWSheadline: BLIZZARD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 6 AM AKST WEDNESDAY

properties.areaDesc: Western Arctic Coast; Northwest Arctic Coast; Northern Arctic Coast
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 9 at 7:33PM AKST until November 11 at 6:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow and blowing snow expected. Total snow accumulations up
to three inches. Winds gusting as high as 55 mph.

* WHERE...Portions of the Central Arctic Coast & Northwest Arctic
Coast.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM AKST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could reduce visibility to a 1/2 mile or less at times. Blizzard
conditions will be intermittently possible to the east of
Utqiagvik, which will be dependent on the severity of blowing snow
& intensity of the snowfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Scattered light snow showers are expected to
continue during this timeframe. Steadier snowfall along with
heavier snowfall rates are expected to start early Tuesday morning
& last through Tuesday. East-northeast winds will increase as we
progress into Tuesday & generally remain stronger through midweek.
Areas to the east of Utqiagvik could intermittently experience
visibilities as low as 1/4 mile from the onset of the snowfall from
around early Tuesday morning into Tuesday evening as both the
snowfall rates & the wind gusts will be higher over that area
during that timeframe.
properties.instruction: Slow down and use caution while traveling.

properties.areaDesc: SW Kenai Peninsula; NW Kenai Peninsula; Skilak Lake
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 9 at 2:07PM AKST until November 10 at 12:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations up to
3 inches and ice accumulations up to one tenth of an inch. Winds
gusting as high as 45 mph, mainly along the Inlet.

* WHERE...NW Kenai Peninsula, SW Kenai Peninsula, and Skilak Lake.

* WHEN...From 11 PM this evening to noon AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Along the coast, gusty winds
could bring down a few tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges
and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous overnight
into early Tuesday morning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The timing of precipitation has changed and
the advisory start time has been pushed back to tonight. For mid to
late this afternoon, expect a brief period of light snow with
little to no accumulation. The evening hours will then be mostly
dry before precipitation moves back in during the overnight hours.
Snow will transition to freezing rain overnight before becoming all
rain with above freezing temperatures Tuesday morning. There is
increased confidence in a quicker warm-up, meaning less snow
accumulation and a quicker changeover to rain. Areas at sea level
will likely see little snow accumulation, with most of the
accumulation expected at higher elevations, including the Homer
Bluffs.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

NWSheadline: WINTER WEATHER ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 11 PM THIS EVENING TO NOON AKST TUESDAY

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 9 at 2:07PM AKST until November 10 at 12:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation likely. Total snow accumulations between
6 and 12 inches. Ice accumulations around a trace.

* WHERE...Richardson Highway from mile marker 60 and south.

* WHEN...Until noon AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Visibility could be
significantly reduced within heavy snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A band of light snow is expected late this
morning before tapering off this afternoon. A second round of
heavier snow is likely this evening through Tuesday morning. The
higher-end snow amounts are expected towards the north side of
Thompson Pass with the lower-end snow totals expected to the north.
Freezing rain potential is decreasing with this system, although it
cannot be fully ruled out. There is a 10 percent or less chance of
freezing rain mixing in with the snow as temperatures look cold
enough for all snow. Tonsina is not expected to see much snow
accumulation from this system.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

NWSheadline: WINTER WEATHER ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL NOON AKST TUESDAY

properties.headline: Blizzard Warning issued November 9 at 2:07PM AKST until November 10 at 12:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions likely. Total snow accumulations between
8 and 16 inches. Winds could gust as high as 45 mph. Visibility
reduced to as low as one quarter mile in blowing snow.

* WHERE...Thompson Pass.

* WHEN...Until noon AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Visibility could be
significantly reduced within heavy snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A band of light to moderate snow is expected
late this morning before tapering off in the afternoon. A second
round of heavier snow is likely this evening through Tuesday
morning. Conditions will begin to improve starting late Tuesday
morning as winds begin to slowly diminish and snow becomes lighter
and more showery in nature.
properties.instruction:
A Blizzard Warning means severe winter weather conditions are
expected or occurring. Falling and blowing snow with strong winds and
poor visibilities are likely. This will lead to whiteout conditions,
making travel very hazardous. If you must travel, have a winter
survival kit with you. If you get stranded, stay with your vehicle.

For the latest road conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 9 at 2:07PM AKST until November 10 at 9:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulation less
than 1 inch. Ice accumulations of a light glaze to a few hundredths
of an inch. Northeast winds gusting as high as 50 mph across parts
of the Matanuska Valley.

* WHERE...Anchorage and Lower Matanuska Valley.

* WHEN...From 11 PM this evening to 9 AM AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Across the Matanuska Valley,
gusty winds could bring down a few tree branches. Some roads and
bridges will likely become slick and hazardous, especially in wind
sheltered areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The timing of precipitation has changed and
the advisory start time has been pushed back to tonight. For mid to
late this afternoon, expect a brief period of light snow with
little to no accumulation. The evening hours will then be mostly
dry before precipitation moves back in during the overnight hours.
Snow will transition to freezing rain overnight before becoming all
rain with above freezing temperatures Tuesday morning. There is
increased confidence in a quicker warm-up, meaning less snow
accumulation and a quicker changeover to rain. Wind sheltered areas
from east Anchorage up the Glenn Highway to Eagle River, Chugiak,
Eklutna, and the Butte will hold on to freezing surface
temperatures the longest, so roads could be icy for the morning
commute.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

little to no accumulation. The evening hours will then be mostly
dry before precipitation moves back in during the overnight hours.
Snow will transition to freezing rain overnight before becoming all
rain with above freezing temperatures Tuesday morning. There is
increased confidence in a quicker warm-up, meaning less snow
accumulation and a quicker changeover to rain.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 9 at 2:07PM AKST until November 10 at 6:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation likely. Total snow accumulations between
4 and 10 inches. Ice accumulations around a light glaze possible.

* WHERE...Interior Kenai Peninsula and Turnagain Pass.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Visibility could be
significantly reduced within heavy snow. Ponding of water along the
Seward Highway is likely due to rain and melting snow overnight
through Tuesday morning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The higher-end snow totals are expected for
Turnagain Pass and Summit Lake areas, where snow will hold on
longer before changing to rain. Any freezing rain that falls will
be short in duration. Valley locations, including Tern Lake to
Moose Pass will see lower snow accumulation and a quicker
transition from snow to rain this evening.
